haiku-low.q1: They see the same message as any request: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent.
haiku-low.q2: The count is 3 or more, so the request is rolled back. No link and no email are created, and the user still sees the same generic message.
haiku-low.q3: It works for 30 minutes. It ends sooner if the link is used, or if a newer link is issued for the account, which sets used_at.
haiku-low.q4: The link is not used up. used_at stays NULL, so it stays usable until it expires, and the form shows an error to retry.
haiku-low.q5: None. All sessions for the user are deleted, including this device. The user is redirected to /login and must log in with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told; no email arrives.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is kept in API memory and placed in the email job's link, which goes into the email. Only sha256(token) is stored in the database.
haiku-low.q8: It computes h = sha256(token) and selects the row where token_hash = h. It is valid only if used_at IS NULL and expires_at > now.
haiku-low.q9: In the password_resets table. The count is the user's rows with issued_at in the last hour, including used or replaced rows, so old rows fall out by time.
haiku-low.q10: Inside the locked transaction, before inserting the new row, its used_at is set to now for every unused link of that user, killing earlier links.
haiku-low.q11: Link burn (used_at set), password_hash update, and deletion of all the user's sessions commit together. The confirmation email is queued after COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: The UPDATE is conditional on used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now with RETURNING user_id. Only one submit gets a row; the other gets 0 rows, rolls back, and sees the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the same 200 message as everyone: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: The count of that user's rows issued in the last hour is already 3 or more, so the request is rolled back and stopped: no link and no email. The user still sees the same generic 200 message.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes (expires_at = now + 30 min). It ends sooner if it is used by a successful submit, or if it is replaced by a newer link (used_at set).
sonnet.q4: Unchanged and still live: not used up, and usable until it expires. The user gets the form again with an error.
sonnet.q5: None. All sessions for that user are deleted, including the current one. No session is created, and the user is redirected (302) to /login to log in again.
sonnet.q6: The email worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs it and drops the job. Nobody is told. The user saw the generic message, and the failed attempt still counts toward their 3 per hour.
sonnet.q7: The API generates 32 random bytes as the token and keeps it in memory. It puts the raw token in the link in the email job (step 8, after COMMIT). The worker sends that job as the email. Only sha256(token) is stored in the DB.
sonnet.q8: It computes h = sha256(token from the URL) and selects the password_resets row WHERE token_hash = h. The token is valid only if the row exists, used_at IS NULL and expires_at > now. Otherwise it is invalid.
sonnet.q9: It is not a stored counter. It is computed on demand as the count of the user's password_resets rows with issued_at in the last hour, including used or replaced rows. Rows drop out when their issued_at is more than an hour old. The periodic cleanup deletes rows older than a day, which does not affect the count.
sonnet.q10: The user's earlier unused links are killed by setting used_at = now on rows where user_id matches and used_at IS NULL. This is step 5, after the rate-limit check passes and the token is generated, before inserting the new row, all within the same transaction holding the user row lock.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the link is burned (used_at set), the user's password_hash is updated, and all the user's sessions are deleted. The "your password was changed" email is queued after COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: The conditional UPDATE sets used_at WHERE token_hash = h AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now, with RETURNING user_id. Only one submit gets a row. The other gets 0 rows, rolls back and sees the expired page.
